newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Russia's Primakov said Chechnya's talks in October.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Primakov said Chechnya's talks in October.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov arrived in Morocco on Sunday for a 48-hour official visit and said talks over Chechnya would resume in October.
Primakov, who is expected to meet King Hassan at the royal palace of Skhirat, 20 km (12 miles) south of Rabat, said he would discuss with the Moroccan monarch international issues including Chechnya.
"Russia is engaged on the path of peace in Chechnya. Talks will be resumed with no doubt in October but there are some elements which should be taken into account," Primakov told reporters.
He said the main elements were:
-- Avoiding armed provocations which could lead to an explosion of the situation in Chechnya.
- All forces and political groups should participate in the coalition government.
- Defining the status of Chechnya in the next five years.

Earlier this week, Russian security chief Alexander Lebed won support from North Caucasus local leaders for a deal that has halted the Chechen war but raised concern in Moscow that it amounts to capitulation to the rebels.
All of the regional leaders at the conference in Ingushetia, a region bordering on Chechnya, approved the plan signed by Lebed and separatist chief of staff Aslan Maskhadov in August.

The deal, which ended 21 months of fighting in the region, followed a series of humiliating defeats for Russian troops. It postponed a decision on Chechnya's future political status by five years and called for Russian troop withdrawals.
King Hassan, who is the current chairman of the Organisation of Islamic Conference (OIC), was among Moslem leaders to support a peaceful solution to solve the Chechnyan conflict.
"Morocco's position was well balanced and this was very important for us. It took into account the humanitarian aspect of the issue...," he said.
Primakov said: "Separatism brings everywhere its negative fruit...It is the enemy of many countries including in North Africa."

By talking about "separatism in North Africa", Primakov was referring to the 17-year old armed conflict between the separatist Polisario guerrillas and Morocco over the Western Sahara territory, officials said.
